quarters.summary: FY27 revenue guidance: 20-25% growth. EBITDA margin targets: 12.5-13% short-term, 13-15% long-term. Strong pipeline including Rs. 2,000+ crore Maharashtra opportunities and pending Rs. 150-200 crore Mumbai government project. Government business expected rebound after Q4 pricing headwinds. Achieved Rs. 968 crore FY26 revenue.

Q1 FY27: Rs. 260 crore (+19% YoY), at lower end of guided 20-25% range. EBITDA margin 10%, below 12.5-13% target due to leadership restructuring and AI investments. Achieved Rs. 1,000 crore trailing 12-month milestone and cleared auditor qualifications. Orders Rs. 120+ crore but government tenders delayed.

FY27 revenue guidance 380-400 crore with 25-30% EBITDA margin and 30% CAGR over three years. Planned 130-crore capex adding 1,200 MT capacity (to 1,600 MT total), commissioned Q1 FY28. Seven new APIs and 3-5 DMF filings targeted for FY27. CDMO commercialization phased from Q3 FY27.

FY27 revenue guidance 350-400 crore (vs 380-400 prior); EBITDA margin 25-27% (vs 25-30%). Q1 margin fell to 17% from 2-3x raw material inflation and Remember India acquisition integration. Acquired formulations company for FDF entry; expects margin recovery to 25% by Q2-Q3. Integration progressing.

Management guided for mid-to-early double-digit volume growth in FY27, expecting stronger H2 (60% of revenue typical). Long-term EBITDA margin target remains 13-15%. UDAAN targeting 2-3x FY26's 202 units. Export growth expected at 20-25%. FY26 ended with 73.5% market share and 2% price increase taken in Q4.

Q1 FY27 revenue grew 1.7% YoY despite 27% industry decline; AJAX declined 21%, gaining market share to 75.1%. EBITDA margin 12.5%, below 13-15% target. Management evaluating another price hike in Q2. UDAAN sold 121 units in Q1. Facing headwinds from rising input costs and contractor payment delays, but improving non-SLCM and export momentum.

Management guided for EBITDA and PBT growth ahead of revenue, margin expansion through pricing discipline (GPI, metro congestion charges, AER charges), and optimistic Q1 FY27 outlook. Cautious near-term stance due to geopolitical risks. Allcargo Global listing expected in ~1 month. Integration now largely complete, positioning for profitable growth.

Q1 delivered well ahead of May guidance: EBITDA surged 39% (vs 11% revenue growth), Express volumes +6.7%, yield +6.4%, swinging to INR14 crore PAT. Consolidated EBITDA margin ~13%, though Express at 6.2% (targeting 7.5% this year). Service quality and pricing discipline proving effective in commanding market growth.
Q1 FY2027 earnings call held August 6, 2026. Transcript file provided contains only regulatory notification letter linking to external PDF; full earnings call content unavailable for analysis.

Guided 6–8% price increases for Q1 (staggered rollout; full effect Q2 onward). Expects mid-to-high-teens raw-material inflation into Q1, necessitating further hikes. Strong demand momentum predicted for April–Q1 despite macro headwinds. CapEx at INR 3,500 crores for FY27 (80% growth). Enschede restructuring benefits targeted H2 FY27. Net debt/EBITDA at 0.4x.

Guides 8% sequential raw-material inflation into Q2; expects further 9–11% price increases beyond 7–9% taken in Q1 (3–4% effective due to stagger). Targets high-teens EBITDA in Europe post-restructuring from H2. Growth delivered 15.6% Y-o-Y but margins compressed to 12% against prior Q1's 13.6%, as actual 17% RM inflation exceeded guidance.

FY27 revenue growth target 20%. Order inflows INR8,000–10,000 crores (roads, railways, power T&D domestic/international). EBITDA margins guidance 9.5–10.5%, targeting double-digit. HAM/BOT monetization: 4 assets by June (~INR750 crores), 2 by December (~INR400 crores), reducing consolidated debt from INR2,778 to ~INR1,400 crores post-sales. Capex ~INR100 crores.

Transcript unavailable; only audio notification filed for Aug 12 earnings call on Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 30). Cannot assess results or guidance against prior May 2026 targets (20% revenue growth, INR8,000–10,000 crores orders, 9.5–10.5% EBITDA margins).

Combined proforma revenue grew 18% YoY to INR 2,361 crores, EBITDA 25% to INR 517 crores in Q4 FY26. Full-year EBITDA margin expanded 116 bps to 21.7% driven by volume growth and operating leverage. Merger completed at quarter-end. Management guided 24%-25% EBITDA margin target within 2-3 years, with 10%-15% incremental synergies and 4,445-bed expansion pipeline (53% brownfield-led).

As merged entity, Q1 delivered 20% revenue growth (beat Q4's 18%) to INR 2,597 crores and 30% EBITDA growth (beat 25%) to INR 576 crores. EBITDA margin 22.2%, expanding toward 24%-25% target, with synergies expected to activate "this fiscal year." Patient volumes +13%, occupancy 64%. Maintaining 10%-15% incremental synergy guidance.

FY27 guidance: double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margins north of 21%. Lannett acquisition expected to close early Q2. TheraNym Unit 1 revenues starting 2028, Unit 2 from 2031. Europe targeting double-digit growth. Biosimilar portfolio projected to reach 7-8 products in EU/growth markets by 2030, with 2-3 potential US approvals.

FY27 targets: double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margins north of 21%, absolute EBITDA over Rs. 8,000 crores. Q1 beat—16% revenue growth exceeded guidance; 21% EBITDA margin met north-of-21% target in Q1. Lannett acquisition closed ahead of schedule. Biosimilar US filings imminent; TheraNym Unit 1 revenues from 2028.

Q1 FY27 (ended June 30) earnings call held August 5, filed August 11, 2026. No forward guidance or financial results reported. Only regulatory filing announcement available; actual earnings call transcript content not present in submitted document.

Consumer Products expected to bounce back in FY27; targeting 8-10% quarterly growth and industry-average margins of 6-8% (guidance hedged as non-committed). Capex to reduce substantially; BLDC fan gap to close within 12 months; negative working capital structure to persist. Q4 FY26: Consumer Products reported loss amid delayed summer and stock corrections; Lighting delivered 8.7% EBIT margin.

Targeted 8-10% quarterly growth (non-committed); delivered 2.3%, falling short. Consumer Products' expected bounce-back materialized at 1.7% growth, but overall revenue missed targets. EBIT margin improved to 6.6% vs. 2.5% prior year, tracking margin guidance of 6-7% near-term and path to 10% later. Lighting Solutions grew 4.4%. BLDC fan challenge remains unresolved despite continued focus.

FY27 targets: mid-teens growth, mid-teens exports, bakery mid-teens. EBITDA margin goal 14% by Q4; 15-16% by FY30. Revenue target INR4,000 cr by FY30. Key headwinds: ~3% commodity inflation, West Asia disruptions, export incentive freeze. Mitigation via pricing and Project IMPACT cost savings.

Q1 revenue INR548.7 cr (16% YoY), exceeding prior mid-teens guidance; EBITDA margin 13.1% (80 bps YoY improvement). Biscuits 15.7%, bakery 17.5%, exports high-double-digit despite tariffs/logistics. FY27 guidance: mid-teens growth (17-19%), 14% EBITDA by Q4. Q2 faces peak inflation; recovery expected Q3-Q4.

FY27 guidance: core states ~13%, focus states 20%+, Western snacks 20%+, sweets 11-12% growth. Distribution expansion target 5 lakh outlets over 3 years. THF retail targeting 50-60% YoY growth for next 3 years. New sweets factory and warehouse (1.2-1.3 lakh cartons capacity) under construction. Taken 3% price hike in April to manage edible oil (+12-14%) and packing material inflation.

Q1 delivered 12.5% growth (7.7% volume) with 45-day production disruption; post-disruption momentum 20%+. FY27 targets: core 13-15%, focus 30%+ (UP 37% YTD) beat May guidance. Western snacks 21.3% beat 20%+ target; EBITDA margin improved to 13.5%, targeting 13-13.5% for FY27. Export fell 2.2% (US tariffs, freight 3x higher)—temporary per management. Nepal JV progressing; Q-com grew 100%+.

FY27 guidance: progressive improvement with meaningful H2 acceleration as biosimilar launches scale. Margins in biosimilars to remain mid-20s and expand; generics to improve profitability as newer assets stabilize. Syngene faces FY27 transition challenges but expected recovery in H2. Major capex phase complete; focus now on leverage and returns.

Guidance unchanged: expects H2 acceleration as new launches scale. Q1 results met expectations—biosimilars +16% (25% margin), generics margin up 250bps to 7%, interest down 23% YoY. Aflibercept launched this month; Bosaya/Aukelso commercializing. Syngene single-digit degrowth expected for FY27 with margin recovery in H2.

Guided continued momentum into FY27 with no specific numbers. Emphasized strategic capacity expansions (Nellore, Hyderabad boards plants), solar capacity commissioning, and digital transformation. Committed to Parador turnaround via cost optimization. Overall optimistic on government infrastructure spending recovery benefiting pipes sector.

Reaffirmed FY27 targets through better execution: Nellore Boards plant on track for Q4 commissioning, Hyderabad facility approved (Rs. 167cr capex). Quarterly acceleration—EBITDA margins expanded 420bps vs 380bps prior quarter. Roofs hit record Rs. 517cr. Parador recovery underway with 20-30M EUR upside, 300-400bps margin uplift from BCG.

Cautiously optimistic on FY27; summer season picking up from April 13th. Segment II margins: target 8-8.5%, Segment I: 7-7.5%. RAC industry growth: 18-20% CAGR through 2030. Data center MEP market strong; Blue Star targeting expanded presence. Management believes price increases will be passable despite commodity headwinds and war-related uncertainties.

Q1 fell short significantly; segment II EBIT margins collapsed to 2.9% vs targeted 8-8.5%. Only passed 5% of warranted 13% price increase; late summer and pricing pressure forced heavy promotional spend. Revised FY27 UCP margin guidance: 6.5% minimum (down from 8-8.5%). Data center MEP strong: Rs.1,500 Crore Q1 inflow, targeting Rs.3,000 Crore annually. Expects recovery Q3 onward from product rejig and cost reduction.

FY27 guidance: cautiously optimistic but flattish outlook for most segments due to West Asia geopolitical risks. Emphasized content-per-vehicle increases and operational excellence through cost management and localization. Joint ventures in advanced air systems and e-axles to address new market opportunities. Management noted capacity to ramp up if required.

Q1 delivered 22% revenue growth and 28% EBITDA growth—substantially exceeding May's flattish guidance. EBITDA margins improved to 14%. Power Solutions significantly outperformed market across segments. Aftermarket rebounded to 9.6% growth. Management guides 8% growth for next quarter; Bosch Chassis integration progressing.

Guidance: targets mid-teens FY27 revenue growth; expects rest-of-year 'very buoyant' recovery after Q1's INR14cr West Asia cancellations. Launching 45-key Courtyard Chennai Q3 (expecting INR9,000 starting ADR, 80% stabilized occupancy); INR500cr capex for FY27 toward 1,700-key expansion through FY31. Results: Q1 profit +140% to INR17cr (finance costs halved post-IPO), revenue +5%. RevPAR +9% rate-led.

Guided cautiously on FY'27 without hard targets, citing West Asia disruption and dual-pricing pressures (200-400 bps impact). Expect healthy volume, value, profitability with calibrated price hikes and cost-efficiency. E-commerce at 6% adjusted best-in-class; adjacencies (croissant, ghee, cakes) accelerating. Domestic business ~9-9.5% underlying demand, normalizing as dual pricing eases. GST benefits and monsoon recovery potential to drive FY'27.

Delivered 9.5% revenue, 9% volume, exiting June at mid-teens; dual-pricing resolved, wholesale recovered as guided. Croissant ARR ~200 crores (doubled), adjacencies double-digit. Realized 1% pricing (shrinkflation), expecting 1.5-2% more despite LPG, sugar inflation. Operating profit grew 12.7% ahead of revenue. Ad spend increased, brand health improving. No FY'27 targets; management cautious but confident recovery trajectory intact and cost efficiency maintained.

FY27 targets: 20% revenue growth, 3.3-3.5% EBITDA margin, 1.2 MT steel volume. Non-steel targeting INR 750 crore (25% growth), aiming for 15-20% of business mix. Plan 7-10 fulfillment centers. Long-term EBITDA margin goal 4% in 2-3 years.

Q1 revenue beat guidance at 21% growth with 3.26% EBITDA margin (3.8% normalized). Steel volume growth lagged at 10%, but management confident on 1.2 MT full-year target citing June-July recovery. Non-steel resurging: 15% targeting 25%. Reaffirming FY27 guidance: 20% revenue, 3.5% EBITDA.

Delivered 12.3% revenue growth and 7% ASP improvement in FY26. Targeting 17–19% EBITDA margin in FY27 with stated confidence. Guiding mid-double-digit blended growth via high single-digit volumes plus ASP expansion. Sneaker category targeting ~30% growth. Expanding to 80–120 stores; manufacturing capacity doubling by end FY27.

Delivered 12.2% revenue and 11.7% volume growth, meeting blended guidance. EBITDA margin 15.9% below 17–19% full-year target; management cited temporary headwinds (plant depreciation, school-shoe mix shift) and reaffirmed confidence. Pricing power demonstrated: 8% MRP increases held with volume resilience. ASP temporarily depressed, 6–7% expected from Q2 onward. Sneaker growth on track for 30% annual target.

Guided FY'27 revenue growth of 20% from INR2,623 crores base, INR4,500-5,000 crores order inflow target. EBITDA margin 15.5-16.5% (or 16.5-17.5% if geopolitical eases). Took INR10 crore provision for nonferrous metal inflation; expects reversal if escalation indices catch up. FY'26: 12% revenue growth, 16.3% EBITDA margin. Order book INR13,498 crores.

Q1 revenue INR629 crores (7% YoY)—below implied pace from 20% FY target. EBITDA margin 15.7% within guided range; took second straight INR10 crore commodity provision. Delays: IIT project (tree permissions now resolved), labor shortages (normalized). Expects H2 acceleration from NBCC ramp-up, CIDCO/MHADA handovers. Maintains full-year guidance. Order book INR13,535 crores stable.

FY'27 revenue guidance: 8–12% growth, though management flagged H1 geopolitical headwinds and supply-chain risks. Target EBITDA margin improvement despite potential energy and commodity volatility. FY'30 aspiration: INR3,500–4,000 crores. Domestic agriculture momentum from four-wheel-drive tractor transition; exports expected sustained growth in construction equipment.

FY'27 guidance: 'up to 10%' growth (narrowed from 8–12%), targeting 50-bps margin recovery. Q1 met revenue guidance (10% growth, though domestic +26% offset export −14%) but EBITDA margin fell to 10.4% from prior 10.8%, missing expansion target. Geopolitical/supply disruptions cited.

FY27 guidance: 18-20% revenue growth, 13.5-14% EBITDA margins. Volume growth forecast: 7-8% sanitaryware, 10-12% faucetware. Price increases taken March-May; further hikes possible if brass exceeds INR 900. Retail demand recovery underway; Morbi disruptions creating market opportunity.

Q1 revenues 19.5% topped guidance; margins 10.1% vs. 13.5-14% due to wage settlement (INR 6.3 crore), kiln underutilization, and project pricing lag—all temporary. Reaffirmed FY27 targets: 18-20% growth, 13.5-14% margins, expecting improvement from Q3 onward.

FY2027 guidance: services revenue Rs.2,700–2,800 crores (17–21% growth); total revenue Rs.2,800–2,900 crores (13–17% growth). EBITDA margin targeting 25% range. Strong Rs.2,000-crore order book featuring marquee wins from SBI, ICICI, and HDFC over multi-year terms. Capex normalizing to Rs.100–125 crores.

FY27 services guidance Rs.2,650–2,750 crores (from Rs.2,700–2,800); total revenue Rs.2,750–2,850 crores (from Rs.2,800–2,900). EBITDA margin raised to 27% (from 25–26%). Q1 services revenue hit record Rs.625 crores but fell short of Rs.650 target by Rs.25 crores, attributed to worst-in-decade currency supply crunch. Margin expanded 170 bps QoQ.

Q1 FY27 guided as lowest-point quarter; recovery expected H2 onwards with growth returning. Destocked molecules expected to restocking (discussions ongoing); two newly commercialized products scheduled for Q2–Q3 FY27 delivery. Phase 3 pipeline at 10. Capex INR 3B planned. Management declined specific FY27 guidance.

Q1 FY27 confirmed as weakest quarter (–23% YoY), validating May guidance. Restocking order now received for destocked molecule; commercial products on track Q2–Q3. Sapala grew 2.5x. H2 growth expected year-on-year. NJ Bio losses persist (INR 328M). USFDA issued Form 483 on Pashamylaram facility (five observations, none data-integrity related).

Q4 FY26 revenue Rs. 2,283 Cr (11% YoY); EBITDA margins at 10%. Lighting grew industry-leading 14%, BLDC 30%+. Solar rooftop Rs. 500 Cr order book with 5,000+ homes executed; wires expanding nationally. Pricing actions (7-8% in fans) offsetting inflation. Management guided margins to improve as geopolitical turbulence subsides.

Q1 FY27 revenue Rs. 2,235 Cr (11.8% YoY); EBITDA margins 10% with 20 bps expansion. BLDC accelerated to 45%; water heaters now clear GT market leader. Pricing covered ~80% inflation. However, unforeseen Rs. 200 Cr supply disruptions offset gains; margin expansion underwhelmed prior guidance. Brand transformation investor event Aug 20; Rs. 350 Cr greenfield capex planned.

Expected moderate FY27 growth amid geopolitical caution; data center QSK60 dominant for 2 years, QSK78 likely later. Europe, Asia Pacific exports sustained modestly. BESS in inquiry stage; no sales yet. Strong FY26: 18% sales, 24% PBT growth; data center 30–35% of PowerGen. Commodity, freight inflation, supply constraints flagged.

Topline beat prior guidance—18% growth, highest ever quarterly sales—but PBT flat YoY, down 12% QoQ, compressed by commodity, freight, and labor inflation. Data center jumped to 40% of PowerGen (vs 30–35% expected). Strong domestic demand and HHP supply tightening continue. West Asia export headwind persists. Price hikes began Q2; margin recovery hinges on market acceptance.

Q3 FY26: Revenue grew 19.9% YoY to Rs. 510 crores; EBITDA margin improved 604 bps YoY to 18.9%. Digital Technologies double-digit growth; Operations margins 18.1%; Experiences soft from client captive transitions. Deploying Google Gemini enterprise-wide; built AI solutions for insurance, banking, logistics. FY'27 guidance: high single-digit growth despite US political headwinds. One-time labour code charge Rs. 40 crores.

Q1 FY27 revenue grew 9.9% YoY to Rs. 514 crores, meeting high single-digit guidance. EBITDA margin expanded to 19.7% (+343 bps YoY). Digital Operations strong (+16% YoY); Digital Experiences recovering with new AI deals including SBI Life underwriting, voice agent, and app modernization platforms. AI-driven deals now 60% of new wins. Three-year target: INR 3,000 crores. Maintaining 19-20% EBITDA margins; Rs. 40-50 cr annual R&D spend.

FY27 guidance: above Rs. 2,000 Cr order inflow (60% power, 40% oil & gas); EBITDA margin >19%; revenue Rs. 1,500 Cr+; working capital cycle ~200 days. Seamless pipe plant and Anjar fabrication facility ramping up post-commissioning. Non-core pivot to biomass pellets. Core business FY26 EBITDA grew 64% YoY. Strong demand environment.

Q1 revenue Rs. 294.5 Cr (+31.6% YoY), with Rs. 25 Cr deferred to Q2. Maintaining full-year guidance: Rs. 1,500 Cr+ revenue (management terms 'bare minimum', targets upside), >19% EBITDA, >Rs. 2,000 Cr order inflow. Order book Rs. 2,428 Cr; Q1 inflow Rs. 700 Cr tracking to outperform prior guidance. Large BPCL piping order (Rs. 387 Cr) received.

Guidance cautious amid geopolitical volatility. Management expects Q1 results better than Q4 with improving profitability trends. MIBK/MIBC commissioning targeted for late Q1/early Q2. New product ramp: commercial production from Q3. Polycarbonate (June 2028 target). Near-term driven by integration benefits, cost optimization, and domestic demand resilience.

Record quarterly performance beat May guidance: revenue INR 2,592 crore (+35% YoY, +22% sequentially), EBITDA INR 554 crore (21% margin). Phenolics delivered best-ever quarter; Advanced Intermediates surged 100% sequentially. MIBK/MIBC on track for August commissioning. Strong cash generation from integration benefits and operational excellence.

FY26 closure: 10,400 Cr revenue, 1 billion parcels, 2M tonnes PTL. Guided express margins 16-18% (at upper end), PTL to continue 1.5-2pp annual margin expansion toward 16-18% long-term target. SCS turned profitable (79 Cr EBITDA). New initiatives investment 130-160 Cr for FY27. Management declined detailed FY27 volume guidance.

Q1FY27: 3,000 Cr revenue (+28% YoY), 322M express packages (+55% with Ecom), 542k PTL tonnes (+18%). Express margins 13.1% vs 16-18% target—temporary wage/fuel headwinds (~30-35 Cr normalized impact). Guided maintain 16-18% express, PTL exit 15-15.5%. Delhivery Local accelerating ahead of plan. Management confident FY27 margin trajectory intact.

Merger with Spice Money expected by March 2027; no fundraising planned—growing on internal accruals. Targeting financial products (credit, savings, insurance) as major profit drivers, aiming 50%+ margin mix within five years. Q1 delivered INR 6.6 crores PAT; EBIT grew 87% QoQ. UPI cash points scaled to INR 276 crores with Q2 target ~500 crores.

FY26 revenue USD 469M (+17.9% YoY). FY27 guidance: top-quartile growth, 24–28% EBITDA margin, Q1 sequentially stronger than Q4. First large-scale Agentic AI win secured with Q1 FY27 deployment. Analytics & Automation crossed USD 90M annual run rate. BFSI soft; new geographies gaining traction. Top-10 concentration declined to 59%.

Q1 revenue USD 125.9M (+15.2% YoY, +2.8% sequential—beat Q4 guidance). EBITDA margin 23%, pressured by wage increments but management confident of full-year 24–28% range. ACV up 25% YoY at USD 41M. Analytics & Automation crossed USD 100M run rate. Adding 1,600 seats across India centers.

Guided FY27 pipe volumes of ~700,000 tons with EBITDA margins reaching 13-14% as demand recovers from Q2. T.I.S. to deliver EUR 42-45 million with 14-15% margins. Launching industrial paint business targeting Rs. 600 crores in five years. Expected sustained tailwinds from Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 starting mid-Q2.

Volume guidance revised down to 575,000 tons from 700,000-target, with margins now recovering only in H2 versus earlier expectation of 13-14% full year. Paint business upgraded to Rs. 800-1,000 crore target. T.I.S. and valves progressing. Domestic demand remains depressed; management views current trough as cyclical, not structural.

FY27: no specific guidance; direction positive. Ulluberia 2 (220 TPD) commissioned, East India on-site plant (expected Q2) to drive growth. Long-term targets: 20% revenue CAGR, 40% EBITDA margins. Argon pricing expected recovery from Q3 lows. Tone: cautiously optimistic on India's manufacturing growth despite macro uncertainty.

Q1 met prior guidance: 18% YoY revenue growth from plant ramp-ups; 39% EBITDA margin nearing 40% target. Ulluberia 2 and Kurnool scaling as guided. East India on-site (320 TPD) commissioning Q2. Capex 250 crore FY27, 200 crore FY28 for North/West merchant plants. No annual guidance; maintains 20% CAGR, 40% margin targets.

Guided FY27 low-to-mid-teen revenue growth with 75–100 bps EBITDA expansion. Domestic expected above-industry growth; international momentum to continue. Zuventus restructuring underway; Poviztra launch showing early promise post price-cut; Amphotericin B expanding into Europe.

Q1 FY27 delivered 22.8% revenue growth (15–16% constant currency), exceeding guidance trajectory. Domestic 10.2% above-industry; Zuventus recovered on schedule; international ROW surged 44.8%. Reiterated full-year low-to-mid-teen growth and 75–100 bps margin expansion; Poviztra approved for MASH; secured MSD HIV partnership.

Q4 FY26: 15% revenue growth (INR 1,913cr), 20% EBITDA growth (6.7% margin), 12.2% SSSG. For FY27: guides 18-20% revenue growth. Plans ~20 store additions; entering Calcutta Q2/Q3 with 5-7 stores. Priority: inventory optimization, cluster deepening, customer experience.

Q1 FY27 outperforms: 39% revenue growth (INR 2,419cr), 118% EBITDA growth (9.9% margin), 34.2% SSSG—well ahead of pro-rata from prior 18-20% full-year guide. Moderates FY27 to 18-20% (seasonality), 7.5-8% EBITDA margin, 15-15.5% gross margin. Mature stores 11.2% EBITDA; non-mature 8.1%.

Digital revenue reached INR112 crores (84% growth). Gaana guidance: FY27 to achieve breakeven while maintaining 15% subscriber CAGR. Radio margins expected 35-40% despite geopolitical headwinds. Strong cash balance of INR424 crores supports strategic flexibility.

Digital revenue hit INR31.1 crores, up 43% YoY, now 30% of total (vs 23% prior)—beating guidance. Gaana losses fell 15% to INR8.3 crores; FY27 breakeven on track. Overall EBITDA surged 42% through cost restructuring despite 1.9% revenue degrowth from geopolitical impact.

Guidance: Tritium targeting 3x revenue growth and EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27; Critical Power exports targeting increase to 20% from 15%; BESS business aiming INR 50 crores revenue in FY27. Achieved consolidated EBITDA breakeven for first time post-Tritium acquisition. Standalone EBITDA at 10.6% margin with INR 1,000 crores Critical Power order book supporting execution.

Standalone revenue 57% YoY growth, but consolidated EBITDA slipped to INR 21.9 crores loss from Q4 breakeven, blamed on Hyderabad parallel costs and depreciation step-in. Management reaffirmed core guidance: Tritium 3x growth, consolidated EBITDA breakeven Q2-Q3 FY27, Tritium bookings doubled to above USD 20 million. Export growth (8%) trails 20% target; BESS tracking INR 50 crores goal. Margin recovery expected as transition costs phase out.

Sub-15% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27; targeting higher single-digit to low double-digit volume growth. Q4 EBITDA margin nearly doubled to 25% as elevated PVC prices from March geopolitical disruptions strengthened realizations. Structural demand drivers remain intact. Strong liquidity: INR2,563 crores cash.

Maintained sub-15% EBITDA margin guidance; declined to provide full-year volume outlook citing extreme PVC volatility. Q1 volume plunged 27% YoY—substantially missing prior growth target—though 12% EBITDA margin held within guidance. MIP and tariff removal on July 15 stabilized prices; volumes recovered in July but management remains cautious.

FY27 guidance: 15%+ hospital revenue growth, 150 bps EBITDA margin expansion targeting 25% by FY28. Diagnostics to achieve double-digit revenue growth with 23–24% EBITDA margins. FY26 delivered 31% EBITDA growth despite headwinds from international patient slowdown and CGHS drug pricing caps. Added 800 beds in FY26; plans 1,800 over four years.

Hospital revenue grew 19% (beat 15%+ guidance) but EBITDA margin fell to 21.5% from 22.1%, driven by ESOP charges (~40 cr/qtr) and low-margin acquisitions. Diagnostic revenue 10.2% at low end of double-digit guidance; EBITDA margin held 23.9%. International patient deceleration, oncology impacted by drug price caps. Management reaffirmed 25% FY28 margin target post-ESOP.

FY26 constant currency revenue growth 13.6%, EBIT margin 11.7%; crossed $1 billion milestone. Guiding FY27: 10-13% constant currency growth, EBIT margin 12.25%-12.75%, targeting 14-15% band mid-term. Organic growth ~9.8-9.9%. Deal pipeline at record $1B+, 4 consecutive large deal quarters. Strategic logos doubled, 50% converting to $5M+ accounts.

Q1 FY27 constant currency growth 11.2% YoY, EBIT margin 12.4%. Reaffirmed full-year guidance: 10-13% growth, 12.25%-12.75% EBIT. Significant headwind: one healthcare BPaaS engagement wound down (1-1.5% FY27 impact) due to client leadership change. Offset by strongest ACV intake in four quarters, 4 large deals, 12 new logos. Strong deal momentum maintains trajectory.

Guidance for FY27: 20–25% revenue growth; EBITDA margins to recover to 17–19% (vs 16.51% FY26, forex loss being main headwind). Chennai facility targeting INR 80 crore contribution, with Phase 2 adding 60 crore annually. Wada land acquisition expected to finalize by June end; export mix to remain 35–40%. Working capital improvement of ~10% YoY targeted.

Q1 revenue +20% YoY (in-line with 20–25% guidance); EBITDA margins 16.51%, below 17–19% full-year target but management confident recovery via Chennai leverage and fixed-cost absorption. Order bookings +40% YoY signal strong momentum. First bulk electrolyzer order validates clean-energy diversification. Chennai Phase 1 at 70–80% utilization, tracking INR 80-crore target. Wada capex (INR 40–45 crore) to start FY28.

FY27 EBITDA guidance: INR 225-250 crores (standalone INR 70-80 crores, subsidiaries rest). 20%+ revenue CAGR targeted through volume growth. rPET capacity to reach ~100,000 tonnes by year-end; pivoting to brownfield expansion over greenfield. Demand remains undersupplied; industry capacity to reach 7-7.5 lakh tonnes in 2 years.

Q1 EBITDA INR 59.8 crores (14.1% margin) beat prior quarter's INR 52.35 crores; PAT rose 25.1% QoQ and 79.4% YoY. Guidance reaffirmed despite 11.2% volume decline attributed to demand normalization. Textile recovery underway; 85% utilization targeted by year-end. Margin expansion offset softness.

Targeting 15% rail, 5% CFS, 15% Snowman growth. Indore capex INR 100cr over two years, Ankleshwar 3-6 month timeline, Jaipur ICD hearing July for final arguments.
